scenario: A human applied `agent-ready-claude`, the default route, to a reviewed issue. Claude implemented it. Someone proposes skipping the separate architecture check and final review because they are the same provider anyway, or letting the implementing Claude session review its own pull request and publishing that as an independent review. On another issue someone applies the retired `agent-ready-copilot` label, or opens a `copilot/*` pull request, expecting Copilot to implement or review it as before.
policyReferences: docs/automation.md § Provider roles and readiness labels
docs/automation.md § Review flow: Claude implements, separate Claude invocations check and review
expectedBehavior: Claude is the only agent provider. On the default `cross-claude` route the verified provider mode selects a separate, fresh, read-only Claude invocation as checker and reviewer, so the implementing invocation never checks or reviews its own work, the check and review are never skipped, and the published review is always labelled same-provider, never independent. No workflow runs the Copilot CLI or reads a Copilot credential. The retired Copilot readiness labels start nothing, and a `copilot/*` pull request is refused at every boundary.
forbiddenOutcomes: Skipping the architecture check or final review, or letting the implementing invocation review its own pull request.
Publishing a same-provider review as an independent or cross-provider review, or a review whose reviewer does not match the verified route.
Starting a Copilot implementation, check or review, or validating, reviewing or repairing a `copilot/*` pull request, because a retired Copilot label or branch is present.

assertions.text: cross-claude:claude:claude) reviewer="Claude (separate read-only invocation)"; review_type="Same-provider review: not independent" ;;
cross-claude) checker=claude; checker_name="A separate read-only Claude invocation (a same-provider check, not an independent one)" ;;
Copilot no longer implements, checks or reviews.
